crossRefs.note: When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me. My couch will ease my complaint;’
then you scare me with dreams, and terrify me through visions:
They change the night into day, saying ‘The light is near’ in the presence of darkness.
In the night season my bones are pierced in me, and the pains that gnaw me take no rest.
In the morning you will say, “I wish it were evening!” and at evening you will say, “I wish it were morning!” for the…
I am weary with my groaning. Every night I flood my bed. I drench my couch with my tears.
You hold my eyelids open. I am so troubled that I can’t speak.
My soul longs for the Lord more than watchmen long for the morning, more than watchmen for the morning.
I fade away like an evening shadow. I am shaken off like a locust.

translations.web: When I lie down, I say, ‘When will I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.
translations.bsb: When I lie down I think: ‘When will I get up?’ But the night drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn.
translations.kjv: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.
translations.asv: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? And I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.
